faq.q: What is the origin of Kazi?
faq.a: Kazi is associated with Arabic. Kazi is Arabic قَاضِي (Qādī) 'judge, magistrate', from the root ق ض ي (q-ḍ-y). CRITICAL SOURCE ERROR: the source gave كاظم (a different name) and glossed the name 'helper, advisor, guide'; the correct form is قَاضِي. Same name as kazim.
Yes — the underlying form قاضي is Arabic.
Kazi can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.q: What does Kazi mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Kazi is rendered قاضی and carries the sense قاضی، منصف.

faq.q: What does Kazi mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Kazi is rendered قاضی and carries the sense قاضی، داور.
A romanized syllable approximation is ka-zi. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Kazi?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Kazi, kazi. Script forms are قاضي, قاضی, क़ाज़ी.

faq.q: Is Kazi a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
